verdict.rationale: AutoGen's human-in-the-loop docs describe a built-in UserProxyAgent that acts as a proxy for a user to give feedback to a team, and AutoGen Studio offers run control with pause or stop. Together these show first-party mid-run human involvement and pausing, but the evidence never shows an approval gate or how a run resumes with the human's decision. A community comment corroborates keeping a human in the loop. Missing for 10: documented approval/rejection gating of agent actions, explicit pause-then-resume semantics carrying the human's decision back into the run, hands-on corroboration of the resume flow.

support.subject: As a developer, I can pause an agent mid-run for human input or approval and resume with the human's decision

citations.quote: The UserProxyAgent is a special built-in agent that acts as a proxy for a user to provide feedback to the team.
Full run control with the ability to pause or stop execution
keep the human and the loop that can assist the agents to solve problems
